newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, US Fed in pact on financial regulation info.
newsitem.headline: Chile, US Fed in pact on financial regulation info.

text.p: The Chilean government and the U.S. Federal Reserve System signed an agreement on Monday to exchange information on ways of regulating the financial sector, said officials.

The pact was signed in Santiago by the William Ryback, the Fed's international supervision associate director, and by the head of Chile's Banking and Financial Institutions Superintendency, Jose Florencio Guzman.
"This type of agreement is aimed at preventing situations like those experienced by (Chile's) financial system in the 1980s," said Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, who was present at the ceremony.
He was referring to the financial crisis in 1982 during which the Central Bank had to bail out many private banks to prevent them from collapsing.
This was the third of this kind of agreement the Fed has signed and the first with a Latin American country, said Ryback.
The first two agreements were with Britain and Germany.
